title: Round 26 West North Central closing and Gulf opening state-frame USGS GNIS source register
scope: All-GNIS starter registers for Minnesota and Louisiana. Every seeded row reproduces one accepted USGS GNIS Geocoder candidate screened by exact official name, returned type/state/county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and returned primary point. Eagle Mountain, Lake of the Woods, and Driskill Mountain additionally carry GNIS Domestic Names per-ID checks.

usgsGeocoder.use: Fuzzy candidate discovery only. A candidate was accepted only when Name, Type, State, County, GnisId, Latitude, and Longitude all matched the intended feature. Parishes, counties, reservations, divisions, census areas, islands, springs, bays, harbors, canals, deltas, air stations, air bases, historical places, and same-name records of another class or county were rejected explicitly where relevant. Punctuation variants (St. versus Saint) were screened both ways and recorded.

gnisDomesticNames.use: Per-ID identity checks for Eagle Mountain (656081 plus rejected 656080 and 643035), confirming the Minnesota High Point description; Lake of the Woods (654378 plus rejected 1930543), confirming the Board decisions and multi-sequence record; Red River of the North (1035890), confirming the river description while the returned primary point sits in Canada; and Driskill Mountain (542199), confirming the Louisiana High Point description.

selectionRules: VERIFIED=1 is claimed only for an exact official name, compatible GNIS feature class/type, intended state and returned primary county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and an official point returned by a cited USGS service.

Grouped Geocoder Types map explicitly to stored row classes: Cities & Populated Places to Populated Place, Lakes & Reservoirs to Lake for the accepted named lakes, Streams & Canals to Stream for the accepted river records, and Summit to Summit.
A stored GNIS primary point is never described as a municipal boundary, street-address geocode, generic centroid, shoreline polygon, summit outline, or river centerline.

If exact-name candidates remain indistinguishable, the state-filtered screen returns no intended feature record, the returned record does not match the intended name and type, or the returned primary point does not identify an in-frame reach of the intended feature, the feature is omitted from that state gazetteer and may appear only as a generalized context corridor.

Statewide frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized corridors; no bundled DEM or surveyed boundary is implied. Louisiana ships a labelled generalized Gulf coast line that is not a shoreline survey.

minnesota.title: Minnesota statewide frame
minnesota.frameNote: West North Central closing batch: the Saint Paul, Minneapolis, Duluth, Rochester, Mankato, Saint Cloud, and International Falls anchors are balanced with per-ID Eagle Mountain (disambiguated from two undesignated same-name summits), the Board-decision Lake of the Woods record, Mille Lacs Lake, Lake Minnetonka, and the Minnesota River. St./Saint spelling gates, the Mississippi reservoir-only screen, the Red River of the North Canada-primary point, and the Lake Superior/St. Croix empty screens are recorded.

identityDecisions.candidate: Eagle Mountain, FEATURE_ID 656081 versus two undesignated same-name summits
identityDecisions.decision: Seeded the Cook County record 656081 after a GNIS Domestic Names per-ID check showed the description Highest elevation in MN at 2301 feet, Located 20 mi NW of Grand Marais, Primary Map Eagle Mountain, and coordinate sequence 1 marked High Point at the stored point. Rejected the undesignated Lutsen-quad summit 656080 and the Todd County Eagle Mountain 643035.
identityDecisions.knownServiceDiscrepancy: The 2026-10-23 Geocoder screen returned all three exact-name Summit records and listed 656080 first; suggestion order is not identity evidence, and only the per-ID description identifies the state high point.

identityDecisions.candidate: Lake of the Woods, FEATURE_ID 654378 versus 1930543
identityDecisions.decision: Seeded 654378: the per-ID check shows Board Decisions making the name official in 1911 and 1953, 18 coordinate sequences around the lake, and sequence 1 matching this screen. Rejected the same-name county record 659483, the single-point 2001 text record 1930543, and the Sherburne County swamp 654379.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The primary point is not the shoreline of the lake, and the rejected 2001 record is not verified as a separate feature.

identityDecisions.decision: Seeded after a GNIS Domestic Names per-ID check confirmed Class=Summit, Primary State=Louisiana, Primary County=Bienville Parish, coordinate sequence 1 at the stored point marked High Point, and the description Highest elevation in LA at 535 feet; the Geocoder returned a single exact Summit record and the coordinate matches.

identityDecisions.candidate: St. versus Saint spelling gates in Minnesota: St. Paul and St. Cloud under states=MN
identityDecisions.decision: Both St.-spelled screens returned empty arrays on 2026-10-23; the Saint-spelled screens returned Saint Paul 662851 (Ramsey) and Saint Cloud 650559 (Stearns). Both Saint records are seeded; the Saint Paul Church/Park/Island pile is rejected in the row note.
identityDecisions.reason: Fourth spelling gate after St. Louis and St. Joseph (round 25): the official GNIS name field uses the Saint spelling, so the punctuation screen is an identity gate rather than a second feature.

identityDecisions.candidate: Mississippi River under states=IA, states=MO, states=MN, and states=LA
identityDecisions.decision: Seeded only in Louisiana at the returned Plaquemines Parish sequence (29.1510582, -89.2533842), FEATURE_ID 1629903, the first seeded Mississippi River row. Iowa returned an empty array, Missouri returned only the Mississippi River Hills Area record 758109, and Minnesota returned only the Mississippi River Reservoir lake 1776673; those frames keep border corridors only.
identityDecisions.knownServiceDiscrepancy: Three distinct failure modes precede the Louisiana success: empty screen, name mismatch, and type mismatch. The Louisiana point identifies the lower river only and does not verify the upstream reaches.

identityDecisions.candidate: Red River chain: ND/OK empty, TX Brown County, MN Red River of the North, LA West Feliciana
identityDecisions.decision: Seeded the Louisiana stream 558728 at the returned West Feliciana Parish sequence (31.0193471, -91.7478975). Not seeded: North Dakota and Oklahoma screens returned empty (round 22), the Texas screen returned a Brown County record rejected in round 24, and the Minnesota screen returned exact Red River of the North 1035890 but without an in-frame primary point.
identityDecisions.knownServiceDiscrepancy: For 1035890 the Geocoder reported the returned primary point (50.4002778, -96.8000000) with County=Kittson County, while the per-ID check marks sequence 1 with no state or map unit because the point sits in Canada at the Lake Winnipeg terminus. Minnesota sequences exist on the record but were not the returned primary, so the Minnesota frame keeps a generalized border corridor only.

identityDecisions.decision: Rainy Lake returned four same-name lake records (Cass 657973, Koochiching 662245 and 1776935, Otter Tail 649799) that the screens do not disambiguate; Calcasieu Lake returned under the Bays & Harbors type 559665. identityDecisions.notClaimed: No exclusion on identity grounds for Calcasieu; Rainy Lake remains ambiguous and is not seeded on identity grounds.

knownLimitations: Minnesota and Louisiana are starter registers, not statewide GNIS extracts. Each contains 12 deliberately selected identity-safe rows.

The USGS Geocoder is a suggestion service; exact-match screening by name/type/state/county/FEATURE_ID is part of the evidence, and the returned county is primary-county provenance. Eagle Mountain, Lake of the Woods, and Driskill Mountain additionally carry per-ID Domestic Names detail checks.

GNIS point data do not supply the displayed terrain or corridors. Both frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized context lines; the Louisiana coast line is generalized, not a shoreline survey.

State frames are rectangles, not state-boundary clipping masks. Both rectangles include small areas outside their state outlines (including Canadian waters north of Minnesota); no boundary geometry is claimed.
